narr: The remains of Tropical Storm Fred moved across central and north Georgia as a tropical depression during the overnight hours through the morning producing isolated reports of damaging winds in convective bands and several tornadoes. No reports of wind damage were received outside of the stronger convective bands. Rainfall amounts exceeded 4 inches in portions of northeast Georgia, with amounts of 6 to 8 inches observed in the northeast Georgia mountains.
ev: The Emergency Manager reported flooding on US-23 near Valley Hills Road and Industrial Avenue, resulting in its closure. Radar estimates indicate that 4 to 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding of Swift Street between Industrial Drive and Whitesville Street due to high water from Oseligee Creek. Radar estimates indicate that |3 to 5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Hamilton Road was closed at Old Chipley Road and Hagler Road due to flash flooding. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

Doraville Police reported the exit ramps Buford Highway to and from I-285 shut down due to high water. Radar estimates indicate that between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager and several media outlets reported flash flooding in the Cleveland area, including but not limited to Campbell Street, Thomas Road at Georgia 115 West, South Main Street, Quillian Street, Cooley Woods at Mountain Meadows, and Ricky West at Mossy Acres. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 8 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager and several Media relayed reports of flash flooding in the city of Helen. Widespread flooding of Edelweiss Strasse and Bruken Strasse occurred due to high water on the Chattahoochee River. Water inundated the patio of a restaurant and caused damage to a bridge by the Chamber of Commerce. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 8 inches of rain occurred over the area during the storm.

The Emergency Manager and several media outlets reported flash flooding over several roads in Sautee Nacoochee, including, but not limited to, Mauldin Road at Asbestos Road, Bean Creek at Gold Valley Road, Asbestos Road and Chastain Road. Radar estimates indicate that 6 to 8 inches of rain fell over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Broadcast Media reported significant flooding along I-85 near Jimmy Carter Boulevard. Parts of the interstate were shut down due to high water over the roadway. Radar estimates indicate that 1.5 to 2.5 inches quickly fell over the area, causing the flash flooding.
